premise: There is no line, no routine and no trick that survives contact with a real person. What works is being someone with a life, saying what you actually want, and letting people say no. This campaign runs on that and nothing else.

reps.label: Opened a conversation
reps.hint: Any stranger, any length. Volume is the point.

reps.label: Showed interest openly
reps.hint: They could tell you were interested. That is the whole rep.

reps.label: Asked for time or contact
reps.hint: A clear ask with a real chance of no.

reps.label: Got turned down
reps.hint: The most valuable rep here. It means you were honest.

reps.label: Met up with someone
reps.hint: A date, a walk, a coffee. It counts.

principles.title: Vulnerability is the mechanism
principles.body: Attraction is not produced by performing a better version of yourself. It is produced by letting someone see the real one while they still have the option to walk away. Every technique that hides who you are removes the only thing that could have worked. If it cannot fail, it cannot count.

principles.title: Build the life first
principles.body: No opener repairs an empty week. The most efficient thing you can do for your dating life is have somewhere to be, something you are getting good at, and people who expect you. That is not preparation for meeting someone — it is the thing itself, and it happens to be attractive.

principles.title: Neediness is an investment problem
principles.body: Neediness is not wanting someone. It is putting your sense of your own worth inside their reaction, so their answer decides how you feel about yourself. You fix it by having enough in your life that one person's no is information rather than a verdict.

principles.title: Polarize
principles.body: Trying to be acceptable to everyone makes you compelling to no one. Have opinions, state preferences, be visibly a specific person. You want the people who are not a fit to work that out quickly — that is the mechanism working, not failing.

principles.title: Say it, do not hint
principles.body: The friendly approach that never states its intent is not kindness, it is risk management, and people can feel the difference. Expressing interest plainly is more respectful than orbiting someone for months: it gives them the information they need to say yes or no.

principles.title: Rejection is the measurement
principles.body: If you are never turned down, you are not being honest — you are only asking where the answer is already certain. Track rejections the way a lifter tracks volume. A month with ten of them is a month you told the truth ten times.

principles.title: No means no, immediately
principles.body: The instant someone declines, it is over, and your job is to make that costless for them. No persuading, no second ask, no sulking. This is not only decency: an ask that cannot be refused cleanly was never an honest ask, and treating no as final is what makes your yes worth anything.

principles.title: You are choosing too
principles.body: Chasing assumes the other person is the prize and you are auditioning. You have preferences, standards and a life you like. Spend your attention on people who are glad you turned up, and let the rest go without a story about what it means.

missions.do: Write down, in one sentence, what you actually want. Not what sounds reasonable.
missions.why: You cannot ask honestly for something you have not admitted to wanting.

missions.do: Go somewhere people gather, alone, for one hour. No phone as a shield.
missions.why: You have to be reachable before you can be met. Presence is step one.

missions.do: Fix one thing about how you present yourself that you have been ignoring.
missions.why: Not vanity. Signalling that you take yourself seriously enough to bother.

missions.do: Put one recurring thing in your week that puts you around new people.
missions.why: A class, a league, a night. Repeated exposure beats any single big night out.

missions.do: Open three conversations today with no outcome in mind.
missions.why: Decouple talking to strangers from wanting something. That is the base rep.

missions.do: Say one opinion out loud today that you would normally soften.
missions.why: Being a specific person is the prerequisite. Bland is not safe, it is invisible.

missions.do: Spend an evening somewhere you would go even if nobody was watching.
missions.why: The life is not bait. Build the one you want and stop auditing it for appeal.

missions.do: Hold eye contact one beat longer than comfortable, five times today.
missions.why: Most interest is communicated before a word. Practise the signal on its own.

missions.do: Compliment two people on something they chose, and then leave.
missions.why: Give with no follow-up. It teaches your nervous system that expression is survivable.

missions.do: Tell one friend you are actively looking. Out loud, no joke to soften it.
missions.why: Saying it makes it real and puts other people's rooms in reach.

missions.do: Start a conversation with someone you find attractive. No agenda beyond talking.
missions.why: The first one is the only genuinely hard one. Everything after is repetition.

missions.do: Keep one conversation going past its natural exit point.
missions.why: Small talk dies at ninety seconds unless someone chooses to keep it alive.

missions.do: Tell someone directly that you find them interesting. Then stop talking.
missions.why: State it and let it land. The silence afterwards is the exposure.

missions.do: Ask one person for their contact details.
missions.why: A clear ask. They may say no, which is the point of this whole phase.

missions.do: Follow up within forty-eight hours with a specific plan and a time.
missions.why: "We should hang out" is not an invitation. A day and a time is.

missions.do: Get turned down once today, deliberately. Ask where the answer might be no.
missions.why: You are training for the no, not against it. Go and collect one.

missions.do: Ask someone out with the word 'date' in the sentence.
missions.why: Ambiguity protects you and wastes their time. Be legible about intent.

missions.do: Approach in daylight — a shop, a park, a queue. Not a bar.
missions.why: Sober, unassisted, no music to hide behind. This is the honest version.

missions.do: Say no to something yourself today rather than going along with it.
missions.why: You cannot receive a no gracefully until you are comfortable giving one.

missions.do: Log five reps in one day. Any mix.
missions.why: Volume day. Nothing profound — just proof you can do this repeatedly.

missions.do: Go on a date, or ask until you have one booked.
missions.why: The campaign is not theoretical. Get the thing in the calendar.

missions.do: On a date, say one true thing you would normally keep back.
missions.why: Dates fail from mutual performance, not from honesty. Go first.

missions.do: Decline a second date you are not actually interested in.
missions.why: Filtering is the skill. Politeness that wastes months is not kindness.

missions.do: Ask someone what they are looking for, and answer it yourself first.
missions.why: Mismatched intentions cost more than rejection ever will. Surface them early.

missions.do: Take a rejection without explaining, negotiating or going cold.
missions.why: How you handle a no is the clearest signal of what you are like to be with.

missions.do: Introduce someone you are seeing to a part of your actual life.
missions.why: Stop running a separate dating persona. Merge the two or one of them is fake.

missions.do: Say what you want from this specific person, plainly, to them.
missions.why: Undefined things stay undefined until somebody is brave enough to name them.

missions.do: End something that is not working, kindly and clearly.
missions.why: Letting it fade is the cowardly version. Say it and mean it.

missions.do: Review your last thirty days honestly. Count the reps, not the outcomes.
missions.why: Outcomes involve other people. Reps are entirely yours, and they are the measure.

missions.do: Pursue the person you actually want, not the one who was easiest to approach.
missions.why: You built the nerve for exactly this. Spend it on someone who matters to you.
